specialFocus.title: The Best Week on Record — Now Finish It: Readiness on Every Move
specialFocus.why: All week we've said excellence lives in the small details. Yesterday the office put a number on it. Matt's review of Oct 22–28 came in, and it's the best week since weekly tracking started in September. Day forms were completed 97% of the time, the highest yet. Trailer inspections hit 98%, also the highest yet. Missed forms went from 57 the week before to 25, cut by more than half. And for the second week running, the auditors found no false PPE entries, no backdated paperwork, no undated JSAs and no old or 'N/A' photos. That's not luck. That's every one of you doing the small things right, one form at a time. There's one gap left, and it's the one we fix this morning: the trailer readiness form. It dropped to 73% and has bounced up and down for four weeks. A form that only gets done some of the time isn't a habit yet. Today we make it one.
specialFocus.standardLabel: The Scoreboard and the One Gap — Straight From Matt's Review
standard: The week, by the numbers (Oct 22–28): day forms 97.3% (219 of 225), trailer inspections 98.3% (58 of 59), and 25 missed forms, down from 57. Day forms came up in every segment: ETX day forms went from 75% to 97%, Comstock from 54% to 100%, supervision jobs from 78% to 88%, and XTO was 149 of 150.

22 of the 40 techs the office ranked had zero misses. Robbie Henigan, Humberto Salazar and Larry Taylor led on seven shifts each, with Nathan Contreras, Ralph Forbes, Jordan Lemmons, Dermont Morgan, Justin Pack, Jimmy Cooper, Jerry Gonzales, Ruben Rojo, Cindy Smith, Michael Ellis and Baldemar Bracamontes all perfect too. Dawson Drake went 19 of 20 on 12 shifts, the heaviest load on the list.

The comebacks are the best part. Every tech on the office's attention list the week before improved. Bryan Medlin went from 22 of 28 to a perfect 11 of 11, Joseph Popillion from 5 of 10 to a perfect 7 of 7, and Bobby Galindo, Dennis Easley and Allen White were all perfect. Allen had missed daily forms four weeks running. Not anymore.

The longer view, Sep 1 to Oct 27: missed trailer inspections fell from 18% in September to 7% in October, JSA problems from 79 notes to 16, and photo problems from 37 to 7. Most improved: Dawson Drake (+39 points), Alfredo Vaquera (+38), Michael Ellis (+30) and Baldemar Bracamontes (+26). Pablo Soto has been perfect every week since Sep 30. Cindy Smith has missed one form in two months.

The one gap: trailer readiness. 44 of 60 (73%) this week, after 82%, 71% and 86% in the three weeks before. It's still nearly 1 in 4 missed in October. SM Energy crews were at 8 of 15 this week. The fix: every time a trailer moves, the readiness form gets done before the truck rolls. Not after, and not 'I'll catch it at the end of the day.'

The small stuff that keeps the streak alive: a JSA on every job, including the short ones and field service. The equipment count in StreetSmart has to match what's actually on location. If StreetSmart won't take your photos or you can't get into the app, call it in and resend. A form you did that never made it to the office counts as a miss.

scenarios.title: Trailer Moves at 2 PM
scenarios.body: You finish one job early and dispatch moves you to a second location across the county. You hook up, you're thinking about the drive and the next crew, and you're gone. That's exactly where the readiness form gets lost: the second move of the day. Caleb, walk the circle through it. When does the readiness form get done on a mid-day move? (Before the truck rolls.) What's on it? Who checks it if you're running two locations? Make it automatic: hitch, walk around, readiness form, then go.

scenarios.title: The Six SCBAs That Were Really Two
scenarios.body: The job in StreetSmart says six SCBAs on site. You count two. Maybe the job was copied from an old one and nobody updated it. But if something goes wrong on that location, the paperwork says six people had air, and only two did. When the count is wrong, fix it in the app and tell your lead before work starts. The paperwork has to describe the location you're really standing on, the same as the Stop Work write-ups we talked about last week.

questions: Best week on record. What's one habit you changed this month that you're keeping?
Your trailer moves twice today. Walk us through exactly when each readiness form gets done.
Medlin, Popillion, Galindo, Easley and White went from the office's list to perfect in one week. What's the one thing that makes paperwork easy to finish on location?
Caleb's question: what did the field teach us this week that the breakroom should know?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: This was the best week since tracking began, and it came from small details done right by the whole crew. Keep it: a readiness form on every trailer move before the truck rolls, a JSA on every job, and counts in StreetSmart that match what's on location. Finish the week the way you ran it.
